title: local-dev-repro-workflow-and-quickstart-outline-draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working outline for a minimal, reproducible local developer flow + quickstart that lets engineers go from checkout -> run -> iterate on SDK integrations (generation, chat, embeddings) in under 10 minutes. The goal is to remove friction for debugging integration bugs and for product/solutions engineers to prototype features without provisioning cloud resources.

Non-goals (for this doc):
- Full user-facing tutorial with screenshots (that lives in docs repo).
- Production deployment instructions.
- Exhaustive platform-specific troubleshooting.

Audience:
- New SDK maintainers and contributors
- Platform/solutions engineers validating LLM behavior locally
- Developer advocates and early adopters building prototypes

High-level success criteria:
- Fresh clone + one command to boot a local harness that serves a small HTTP shim mirroring the Redwood API used by customers.
- Repeatable test fixtures that run against both local runner and hosted API with the same test suite.
- Clear failure-mode messages and a short checklist for local troubleshooting.

Quickstart flow (developer path):
1) Prereqs: node 20.x or python 3.11 (pick one for the SDK language), docker installed, git.
2) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk && cd sdk/examples/local-runner
3) ./dev-setup.sh (installs deps, creates .env.local.template -> .env.local)
4) docker-compose up --build (starts small containerized model shim + local telemetry collector)
5) yarn start:example or python examples/run_quickstart.py (issues a few sample requests; shows streaming + function call examples)
6) open http://localhost:8080/health and http://localhost:8080/playground (simple UI to try prompts)

Notes on step components:
- dev-setup.sh: copies env template, optionally creates a local-api-key for the shim, ensures node_modules or venv is present. Keep idempotent.
- docker-compose: two services: model-shim (tiny server that returns canned responses + supports token delays) and telemetry-proxy (captures request/response pairs into logs/test-fixtures). Compose file should work on Apple silicon + Linux (use platform: linux/amd64 where necessary).

Local reproducibility details:
- Model shim design: a pluggable server that can read canned responses based on example IDs and can optionally emulate latency and chunked token streaming. Implementations: Node/Express and Python/FastAPI variants so SDK maintainers can run in their language of choice.
- Deterministic fixtures: fixtures/*.json contains deterministic inputs + expected outputs for the local runner tests. CI can run the same fixtures against hosted API (with a mode flag that accepts variable outputs via a fuzzy matcher).

Developer ergonomics and commands (proposal):
- ./dev-setup.sh --language node|python --force
- make dev-up (wrapper for docker-compose up)
- yarn example:chat || python examples/run_chat.py
- yarn test:local (runs jest/pytest against fixtures using LOCAL_API_URL)
- ./dev-replay-fixture fixtures/simple-chat.json (replays request sequence against local shim and prints diff)

Common failure modes & troubleshooting checklist (quick):
- 502 from local shim: check docker logs (docker-compose logs model-shim), confirm .env.local exists and LOCAL_API_KEY matches sample.
- Streaming stalls: confirm model-shim PACKAGE_STREAMING flag is true; try smaller max_tokens.
- Auth errors from SDK: set LOCAL_API_URL env var before running examples, restart process to pick up env.
- macOS / M1 issues: ensure docker-compose image uses linux/arm64 when necessary or use mutagen for volume mounts.

Telemetry and observability hooks for local runs:
- telemetry-proxy should optionally store request/response pairs to local/telemetry.log and provide a small /metrics endpoint that returns counts by endpoint/model.
- Example SDK should expose a DEBUG=redwood:sdk env var to print wire-level traces (requests, headers masked).

Testing harness ideas:
- Cross-runner test script: tests/run_fixtures.py that parameterizes a fixture runner against two base URLs: LOCAL_API_URL and HOSTED_API_URL. Use fuzzy matchers for text generation (levenshtein threshold, token-level overlap) and strict checks for structured outputs (function call names and JSON shapes).
- Integration smoke test: CI job that runs the fixture suite against the local runner docker image to validate examples before merging doc or examples changes.

Onboarding checklist for new SDK contributors (one-pager summary):
- [ ] clone repo && run ./dev-setup.sh
- [ ] bring up docker-compose and confirm /health
- [ ] run example script and watch telemetry log for 3 successful calls
- [ ] run yarn test:local or pytest -k quickstart and confirm green
- [ ] open PR with a small readme change demonstrating the quickstart flow

Edge cases / open questions (TODOs):
- How to represent nondeterministic generation differences in fixtures without adding fragile golden files? Proposal: store expected structured pieces + fuzzy matcher config per fixture. ACTION: Evan to prototype matcher lib (ENGSDK-842).
- Should the examples use full streaming by default? Harder to test. Proposal: streaming off by default in fixtures, with one streaming-specific fixture.
- Right balance between the model shim fidelity and maintenance burden. Keep shim intentionally simple, expand only when necessary.
- Concurrency testing: do we want the local runner to simulate multiple concurrent requests to catch race conditions? Maybe optional mode --load-sim=10.

Follow-ups / next steps (short roadmap):
1) Prototype minimal node model-shim (2 days) — owner: Liam.
2) Add pytest/jest fixture runner + example fixtures (3 days) — owner: Sofia.
3) Wire telemetry-proxy to write artifacts that CI can ingest (2 days) — owner: Evan.
4) Draft user-facing quickstart in docs repo that mirrors these commands (1 day) — owner: Aisha.

References & links:
- GitHub examples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/main/examples/local-runner
- Confluence concept doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/12345678/SDK+Guide
- Jira: ENGSDK-842 (matcher prototype)

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep examples small: single-file per language if possible.
- Prioritize reproducibility over fidelity: deterministic fixtures > perfect model behavior.
- Consider a small browser-based playground that uses the local runner for demos on PRs.
- Add a short video screencast later for onboarding page.

-----
End of draft.
